title: Blueprint of Ruin
teaser: On the silent cost of success: restless minds, lost connections, and the ruins behind every celebrated triumph.
lines: If sanity is the first thing to go,
then genius must be forged in madness.
If love is lost along the way,
then ambition must be written in solitude.
If heavy eyes bear the fruits of passion,
then insomniacs must be minting empires.
If comfort slows the climb,
then hunger must be the sharpest spur.
If vengeance is a motivator,
then most entrepreneurs must be arsonists.
If betrayal oils the gears of progress,
then empires must run on spilled blood.
If history is written by the victors,
then every textbook is a eulogy in disguise.
In the end, success isn’t a victory—
it’s the last man standing in a field of graves.
closing: Ruins are not always left behind—they are built, step by step, by those who dare to rise in spite of everything.

title: The Fire You Never Saw
teaser: Some flames burn in silence, leaving only ash.
lines: You loved a writer—
how could you ever believe you'd leave unmarked?
Every accusation, every blade of a word
drove me deeper into silence,
while the walls and the night sky
stood as my only witnesses.
You said I wasn’t enough,
that I didn’t try hard enough—
but if only you had seen
the tempests raging through
the hollow corridors of my mind.
I knew I wasn’t the kind
to set your heart ablaze at first glance.
My edges never glittered,
but I stayed, foolishly believing
my depths might one day anchor you.
You sat astride your high horse,
surveying the fragile kingdom
of your own making,
while I drowned quietly in the ruins
of mine.
How effortlessly you brushed off my sorrows,
like ash clinging to your sleeve.
How swiftly you branded my struggles
as burdens you never asked to bear.
Each night, I stitched together dreams of us,
while you built a future
that had no room for my name.
History may call me naive,
but only hearts that burn this deep
ever feel love’s true flame keep.
Still, I do not curse you.
May your days stretch golden,
and your nights be gentle.
May the fire in your eyes
finally learn to burn inward—
for I loved you with a flame
that devoured my soul,
and you never even saw the fire.
closing: We are all ghosts of the fires we survive.

title: When the Devil Holds the Leash
teaser: Between sleepless nights and burning dreams lies a truth you can't unsee.
lines: My eyes are heavy, but my mind won’t shut up.
There’s more here than anyone sees.
This blurriness feels like an omen—
a warning of sleepless nights
where even my will starts to slip away.
It always begins small.
A spark, nothing special, almost invisible.
Then it grows,
feeding on every dream, every bruise,
until it burns like an ancestral flame,
a promise of something bigger—
maybe glory, maybe ruin.
But it’s all still imaginary.
If success were easy,
it would sit on a shelf with a price tag.
Some are born holding it like inheritance,
while others grind themselves to the bone
and still disappear in the crowd.
Life was never fair to begin with,
But these circumstances make it unbearable.
What becomes of a society
when its preachers are corrupt?
When felony parades as justice?
Righteousness looks golden on paper,
but in reality, it’s a mask—
a false hymn sung
for the real diablos to revel in.
Success never comes with guarantees.
Deliverance rarely arrives.
’Cause when the devil holds the leash,
even angels forget how to fly.
closing: Every dream is a bargain struck with the dark.

title: A Quiet Ascent
teaser: On learning that mercy isn't always gentle, and flight isn't always freedom.
lines: Most wings are destined to be clipped,
their fate running deeper than their desires,
their destinies intertwined with their own misfortunes.
You can either have your wings clipped,
or be like Icarus—
these are the options that prevail.
But how can a novice,
an impressionist in heart,
seal their fate with the undulations of nature?
Why can’t they trace the boundless skies
without being scorched by the sun’s unyielding wrath?
Why can’t they rise from their own ashes
like a phoenix crowned in flame,
its wings carved from the embers of its own undoing?
Being extraordinary isn’t the only triumph,
being benevolent isn’t the only form of mercy.
You can wield your own Excalibur
and let its blade rest in quiet command—
not towards your enemies,
but towards yourself.
For sometimes, the fiercest mercy
is the ruthlessness you spare for your own heart.
closing: Maybe the point was never to escape gravity, but to make peace with the way it keeps us from burning.
